findings.quote: Plural agreement can stress the separate members, especially in British English.
findings.problem: The lesson teaches collective nouns treated as separate members, but the only worked collective-noun task (#3) tests an American-English group acting as one. The distinct member-based plural case still has no worked example.

L23.note: No illustration or placeholder occurs; sentence analysis does not depend on a figure.

checked: Subject and verb are defined before agreement. Singular/plural and person precede form rules; phrase and head precede intervening-phrase analysis. Filipino pandiwa, paksa, aspekto, pokus, pananda, and parirala are explained before their application. Actor and affected-object meanings are given before the focus solution uses them.

English number and person are demonstrated with be, have, and third-person verbs; subject-head finding has a concrete question method. Filipino aspect uses action status, focus uses the ang-marked topic and its role, and ng/sa use whole-sentence meaning. Examples #9–#13 apply those methods.

The lesson qualifies collective agreement by meaning and English variety, and and-subject agreement by whether there are separate entities. It qualifies variable indefinite pronouns by reference and mixed or/nor by nearer subject. Filipino aspect cautions against using time words alone or copying kain patterns to every verb; markers are given multiple roles.
